verdict_reason: Codex adversarial consultation surfaced 5 FAIL-graded issues (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5) plus 1 WARN (Q6) and 1 mixed (Q7) on the BA spec. Three of the FAILs are blocking risks that materially threaten the user's stated requirement (one-shot complete codex parity + restart/save/watcher integration). Specifically: (a) AC1's sandbox-verification path can pollute shared /root/.codex/sessions/ which belongs to production codex (CLAUDE.md production isolation violation risk), (b) M4 prescribes a hard schema break across multiple in-repo consumers without compat fallback AND ignores existing gemini/openclaw flavors in the codebase (will break non-codex sessions), (c) M8's restart-script edits read schemaVersion=2 fields but production daemons (default, jade) still run pre-M4 code — produces silent claude-UUID drops or hard failures. Plus AC3 fault-injection wording is technically infeasible in Vitest/Node and will confuse dev. BA must revise.

findings.issue: AC1/AC2 say verification via 'happy codex against the dev daemon (sandbox or manual user-restart-only)' but a sandbox daemon CANNOT isolate codex's shared rollout dir at /root/.codex/sessions/. Real codex run in sandbox will pollute production codex state.

findings.issue: AC3 says 'simulate SIGKILL between truncate and write (test via fault injection in unit test)' — but (a) the atomic writer should NOT truncate the target (it writes to .tmp, fsyncs, renames), and (b) Vitest/Node has no mid-syscall fault injection.
findings.evidence: Codex Q2 FAIL: 'AC3 wording is misleading. Replace with: fault before rename → target remains old; fault after rename → target is old or new, never partial; orphan temp files tolerated/cleaned'.
findings.remediation: Rewrite AC3 to test the SEQUENCE: writer writes to .tmp → fsyncs → renames → fsync parent dir. Fault model: 'if writer is killed before rename, target file is unchanged. If killed after rename, target is the new file. Never zero-byte.' Tests assert step ordering via mocked fs or real temp dirs.

findings.issue: M4 says '/list schema v2 with flavor: claude | codex required + audit jq consumers in same commit, no compat fallback'. But (a) flavor enum is hard-restricted to 2 values while the codebase ALREADY has gemini and openclaw flavors (createSessionMetadata.ts:90, runGemini.ts:128-130, runOpenClaw.ts:159-160), (b) hidden consumers exist: happy-agent integration test (packages/happy-agent/src/happy-agent.integration.test.ts:311-323), openclaw integration test (packages/happy-cli/src/openclaw/openclaw.integration.test.ts:423-429).
findings.evidence: Codex Q4 FAIL with concrete grep evidence of additional consumers and gemini/openclaw flavors. Verified by direct grep of happy-cli/src for notifyDaemonSessionStarted — appears in runGemini.ts and runOpenClaw.ts.
findings.remediation: Either (a) broaden flavor enum to claude|codex|gemini|openclaw|unknown (covers existing reality), OR (b) make flavor strictly optional with claude as implicit default. Audit must include happy-agent and openclaw integration tests, not just controlClient.ts and recovery script. Consider keeping schemaVersion as additive (consumers tolerate its absence) rather than mandating same-commit audit-or-break.

findings.issue: M8 edits to /root/bin/happy-restart.sh would read /list v2 schemaVersion=2 fields. But happy-restart.sh runs against ALL THREE daemons (default, jade, dev). Production daemons still run pre-M4 happy-cli binary returning v1 /list. Without a runtime guard, restart-script will either fail or silently drop claude UUIDs.
findings.evidence: Codex Q5 FAIL: 'critical runtime mismatch risk. If schemaVersion !== 2, fall back to existing claude-only v1 behavior. Never drop existing claude UUID capture because codex fields absent.' This directly threatens user verbatim part 2 (restart/save/watcher monitoring).
findings.remediation: AC6 must add: 'restart-script MUST detect /list schema version. If v1 (no schemaVersion field), use legacy claude-only capture path UNCHANGED. If v2, capture both claude UUIDs AND codex tids. Schema-version mismatch MUST NOT drop claude entries.' Add a guard test in AC6.

findings.issue: M2 says flock is 'optional', M3 writes mapping file from multiple codex wrapper processes. Atomic rename prevents partial-write reads but does NOT prevent lost read-modify-write updates between concurrent writers.
findings.evidence: Codex additional finding: 'M2/M3 locking inconsistency. Make writer locking mandatory, or make the daemon the single mapping writer via /session-started.'
findings.remediation: Either (a) make flock(LOCK_EX) mandatory in M2 around the read-modify-write window for codex-mapping.json, OR (b) restructure so the daemon is the single writer of codex-mapping.json (codex wrappers send tid via /session-started, daemon writes mapping). Option (b) is simpler and aligns with daemon-as-SSoT.

out_of_scope_observations.observation: Multi-backend (gemini, openclaw, acp) all call notifyDaemonSessionStarted. If 'flavor' is added to /list, the existing backends should also be tagged — otherwise codex-only flavor produces ambiguity ('claude or unknown?'). This is a 'should we generalize the flavor enum NOW' question that codex flagged out-of-scope but is relevant to the M4 design.

AC3 also references 'fsync the parent directory'. On many filesystems (tmpfs, NFS) parent-dir fsync is a no-op. Unit tests using tmpfs may not exercise this code path. Worth documenting in dev technical hints.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Q1 FAIL: sandbox is unsafe — shared /root/.codex/sessions/ pollution risk. Q2 FAIL: AC3 fault-injection wording technically infeasible in Vitest. Q3 FAIL: persistence.ts refactor doubles cycle risk; out of cycle. Q4 FAIL: schema-break consumers wider than BA claims (happy-agent, openclaw integration tests); flavor enum ignores existing gemini/openclaw. Q5 FAIL: restart-script mixed-version daemon risk requires schemaVersion guard with legacy fallback. Q6 WARN: BA overclaims codex's resumeExistingThread.ts discovery — architect did name codexAppServerClient.ts:856 (call-chain location); codex's contribution was the wrapper site with session context (actionable). Q7 FAIL for persistence refactor; PASS for codex-mapping atomicity only. Additional: M2/M3 locking inconsistency — make flock mandatory or make daemon the single mapping writer.
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: Findings F1-F8 above are direct mappings from Q1-Q7. Verdict elevated from likely-ACCEPT_WITH_OBSERVATIONS (my pre-codex assessment) to REJECT after codex surfaced two production-isolation risks (F1 shared codex rollout dir; F5 mixed-version daemon). Ba-iteration prescription embeds codex's revised wordings verbatim where they map to actionable AC edits.
